  • Analyze complex business datasets using exploratory data analysis techniques to uncover trends patterns and anomalies that directly inform strategic decisions and operational improvements across the organization.

  • Design and maintain advanced Excel workbooks and macro driven solutions that automate repetitive tasks improve data accuracy and significantly reduce manual processing time for stakeholders.
  • Build interactive Tableau dashboards and visual analytics that clearly communicate key performance indicators helping business partners quickly understand results and act on data driven recommendations.

Selection and Interview Process at Cognizant

The interview process at Cognizant typically consists of three stages: an aptitude test, a technical assessment, and finally, an HR interview for applicable roles.

1. Online Assessment: Shortlisted candidates may first be asked to complete an online assessment covering quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, data interpretation, SQL, and basic programming or analytical problem-solving. For fresher or trainee positions, the assessment may focus more on fundamental SQL, analytical reasoning, and basic data concepts.

2. Technical Interview: The technical round is usually the most important stage. Candidates can expect questions on SQL, Excel, Power BI, Python, statistics, data cleaning, and database concepts. SQL questions may cover joins, WHERE vs. HAVING, subqueries, aggregate functions, window functions such as RANK() and DENSE_RANK(), duplicate records, NULL values, and query execution order.

3. Project Discussion / Case-Based Questions: Interviewers may ask candidates to explain their academic, personal, or professional data analytics projects. You should be prepared to describe the dataset, data-cleaning techniques, tools used, challenges encountered, analysis performed, and business insights obtained. Some interviews may also present a real-world scenario and ask how you would analyze the data and communicate your findings to stakeholders.

4. HR Interview: The final HR discussion generally focuses on career goals, communication skills, availability, location/relocation, compensation, and overall fit. Candidates may also be asked about their strengths, weaknesses, willingness to work with clients or teams, and why they are interested in the Data Analyst role.
